system.name: WINGS
system.one_liner: A multimodal LLM with visual and textual learners in parallel with each attention block, keeping text-only skills while learning multimodal ones.

content.variant_note: chat cards on both sides of a central radar chart; three coloured headings name text-only, interleaved and multimodal instructions
content.argues: WINGS answers well in all three input modes, text-only, interleaved image-text and multimodal, and its radar polygon covers the baselines on both text-only and multimodal benchmarks.
content.subject: A watermelon conversation as chat cards, with a radar chart over 18 benchmarks comparing WINGS, LLaVA-Next and DeepSeek-VL.

lessons.what_to_learn: Show behaviour and score in one teaser: chat cards on both sides, headed by coloured highlighter labels for the input types, around a central radar chart; set key words of the model reply on solid green so the reader sees what it got right.
lessons.suits: papers on chat models or multimodal LLMs that claim balanced capability across input types and have a summary chart over many benchmarks.

WINGS excels in handling text-only tasks while improving performance on visual-related instructions.

summary: WINGS is a multimodal LLM that adds visual and textual learners in parallel with each attention block so that it keeps its text-only skills while learning multimodal ones. Figure 1 is a teaser that sets chat cards on both sides of a radar chart. Three coloured highlighter headings name the instruction types: Text-only Instruction, Interleaved Image-Text Context and Multimodal Instruction. Each card has a speech-bubble user turn over a WINGS reply box in which key words sit on solid green; watermelon photos serve as images. The centre radar compares WINGS, LLaVA-Next and DeepSeek-VL over nine text-only and nine multimodal benchmarks, with WINGS in dark green.
summary_zh: WINGS 是在注意力层并联视觉与文本学习器的多模态大模型，既保留纯文本能力又学习多模态。图 1 在雷达图两侧放置对话卡片，三色高亮标题区分纯文本、图文交错和多模态指令，雷达图比较 WINGS 与两个基线在 18 个基准上的表现。
notes: Prior labels listed scope-overview (benchmark-dashboard); the radar is a result chart, not a map of a task space, so scope-overview is dropped and the chat cards are kept as a real-io-trace walkthrough. The unheaded card at the top right is read as the follow-up of the interleaved context from its green tint and its reply about the left one. The radar polygons seem to be placed as clipped bitmaps with live axis labels.
